To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concept of self-kindness in the context of eating is poorly understood, and the term is not associated with eating healthily, or with self-care.
the participants in our study did not describe eating as a way of being kind to themselves.

the participants described a number of different ways of treating themselves with food and with pleasure in eating described in terms of social eating rather than food, and the participants largely eschewed dieting, but engaged in highly regulated and restricted eating, and the participants did not describe self-kindness in terms of physical health behaviors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between self-kindness, mindful eating, wellbeing and the role of mindfulness-based interventions in improving eating behaviors and wellbeing.
how people make decisions about what they eat, how and why they eat, and the impact of this on their wellbeing.
how people make sense of their eating behaviors and their understanding of self-kindly care of their body and mind.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study suggest the need for a deeper understanding of the relationship between self-kindness and health behaviors and the potential for mindfulness-based eating programs.
there is a lack of clarity around the concept of self-kindness in the community, and that this is a potential barrier to engagement in mindful eating interventions.
the participants described a lack of connection to the notion of self- kindness, although positive eating and other health behaviors were undertaken.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants in this study did not describe eating in the same terms as mindfulness and self-kindness, which are the focus of mindfulness-based eating interventions.

participants in this study were unable to relate self-kindess to eating, and were unable to relate the concept of self-kindess to their own eating behaviors, and that the concept of self-indulgence was associated with self-kindness.
participants described a range of eating behaviors, which were not associated with self-kindness, and that the term self-kindness did not resonate with them as a means to improve wellbeing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-kindness is a difficult concept and that it is not easily connected to physical health behaviors.
self-kindness is a complex construct, and that it is not easily understood or applied in the context of eating and weight regulation.
the notion of self-care, self-regulation and self-kindness needs to be further developed to support the development of mindful eating interventions.
